method: Contact-masked / structure-residualized DCA (conformational-ensemble mask + matched null)
improves_long_range: Does not improve detection; it is the correct subtraction. Establishes how much distal signal survives removal of proximity in any accessible conformer. Published rates: 25% of top couplings >5 A and 3% >15 A over ~4000 families (Anishchenko 2017); ~12% unexplained by any AlphaFold model of family members over 2012 families (Karamanos 2023).
validation_type: CONTACTS (by construction - it is a structural subtraction). Downstream allosteric-pocket ranking validated functionally in La Sala 2023 (all known allosteric pockets in top 3 for 5 proteins incl. p38-alpha).
kinase_evidence: p38-alpha included in La Sala 2023 structure+coevolution+dynamics model. Anishchenko 2017 and Karamanos 2023 are family-generic. Anishchenko 2017 is a KINASE-RELEVANT NEGATIVE in effect: little evidence for direct coupling between spatially separated allosteric and functional sites, or enrichment on putative allosteric pathways.
feasibility: Trivial. Distance matrices over 1M17 + ErbB PDB ensemble + AF models, masking, and permutation nulls. Minutes to hours on 8 cores / 8 GB. Already half-built in this project.
inputs: Scalar APC-corrected scores + structural ensemble (1M17, ErbB-family PDBs incl. asymmetric dimer, AF model, MD average). No J tensor required.
failure_modes: The mask IS the result: too permissive and everything survives, too strict and nothing does. Anishchenko 2017 shows most apparently distal pairs are contacts in some homolog/oligomer, so a single-structure mask is indefensible. Requires separation- AND distance-matched null (coupling decays with both) plus a phylogeny-preserving resampling null (Rodriguez Horta 2021) because phylogeny-induced spurious couplings are comparable in size to the first false positives.
hostile_reviewer: 'Your distal pairs are contacts in the asymmetric dimer or in an ErbB conformer you did not model' (Anishchenko 2017); 'your null is not distance-matched so you are measuring the contact-distance decay'; 'at your median separation of 32 you are in the regime where phylogenetic couplings dominate'.
cost_benefit: Highest payoff per unit cost. Directly answers the reviewer whether the answer is positive or negative.

improves_long_range: Yes for COLLECTIVE functional organisation, which is the defensible reframing. SCA targets quasi-independent groups of coevolving residues rather than pairwise contacts (Halabi 2009; Rivoire 2016).
validation_type: FUNCTIONAL / EXPERIMENTAL - the strongest of any method here. Double-mutant thermodynamic cycles in PDZ (Lockless 1999); complete single-mutation DMS of PSD95-PDZ3 showing sector positions are mutation-sensitive and adaptation initiates only within the sector (McLaughlin 2012); deep coupling scan measuring thousands of pairwise couplings, which SCA quantitatively captured (Salinas 2018); generative validation by artificial WW domains (Russ 2005) and designed chorismate mutases (Russ 2020).
kinase_evidence: DIRECT PRECEDENT. pySCA on the human kinome gave 5 ICs resolving into 3 quasi-independent sectors - catalytic, substrate-specificity, regulatory; catalytic sector enriched for somatic cancer mutations, regulatory-sector residues contact allosteric kinase inhibitors (Creixell 2018). Critically, that study used only 389 human kinases = 265 EFFECTIVE sequences; this pipeline has N_eff = 27,613, ~100x deeper, so it is far better powered than the published kinase SCA.
feasibility: Easy. L=253, N=32,672. SCA 4D array L^2 q^2 = 226 MB float64; Frobenius compression to 253x253; ICA and randomised-alignment nulls are the bulk of runtime. Comfortable on 8 cores / 8 GB.
inputs: Raw MSA + reference sequence for numbering. Does NOT need the J tensor or structures.
failure_modes: Tesileanu 2015: for single-sector proteins SCA output is dominated by sequence conservation and conservation alone gives statistically equivalent functional predictions. Sector count depends on the ICA component choice and on alignment construction. Phylogenetic clades can masquerade as sectors (Colavin 2022).
hostile_reviewer: 'Your sector is just the conserved catalytic core - show me conservation-only gives a different answer' (Tesileanu 2015). Mitigation: the kinase domain demonstrably carries multiple sectors (Creixell 2018), which is exactly the regime where the Tesileanu critique is weakest; run and report the conservation-only control explicitly.
cost_benefit: Best evidence-to-cost ratio. Moves the manuscript's claim from pairwise long-range coupling (poorly supported) to sector organisation (experimentally validated, kinase-precedented).

method: Site-anchored / aggregate coupling profiles to a reference site (KeyAlloSite-style)
improves_long_range: Yes, by changing the statistic: aggregate coupling of each candidate pocket to the orthosteric site rather than individual pair ranks. Allosteric sites were found strongly coupled to the orthosteric site relative to non-functional sites, and the signal lives in WEAK couplings that pairwise top-N ranking discards (Xie 2023).
validation_type: FUNCTIONAL / literature-annotated allosteric sites and key cancer mutations; agreement with prior experimental studies for BCR-ABL1, Tar and PDZ3 (Xie 2023). Not validated against double-mutant cycles directly.
kinase_evidence: DIRECT PRECEDENT: BCR-ABL1, a tyrosine kinase with the canonical myristoyl allosteric pocket, is one of the three worked examples in Xie 2023.
feasibility: Trivial. Aggregation over the existing 253x253 APC-corrected score matrix. Minutes.
inputs: Scalar scores + pocket/site definitions (ATP site from erlotinib contacts in 1M17; candidate allosteric sites: alphaC-out pocket, C-lobe asymmetric-dimer interface, juxtamembrane docking surface). No J tensor.
failure_modes: Entirely determined by how the anchor and control sets are drawn. Highly conserved anchors inflate coupling to everything, so an entropy/conservation control is mandatory. Needs matched non-functional control pockets of equal size and equal mean conservation, as in Xie 2023.
hostile_reviewer: 'You picked the allosteric pocket after seeing the coupling map.' Mitigation: define all sites from independent structural and pharmacological evidence before computing, state them in Methods, and include decoy pockets.
cost_benefit: Near-zero cost, direct kinase precedent, and it produces exactly the orthosteric-vs-allosteric contrast the manuscript's Figure 7 needs.

method: Hopfield-Potts / low-rank spectral decomposition of the Potts coupling matrix
improves_long_range: Partly. The literature establishes the split, not its allosteric meaning: low-eigenvalue modes are highly localised and map to 3D contacts while top modes are collective and are discarded by PCA (Cocco 2013); 20-40 Hopfield patterns give a close-to-generative model but their distributed collective nature intrinsically limits contact-map prediction (Shimagaki 2019). Independent theoretical support for stripping top modes: phylogeny produces a power-law tail in the covariance spectrum and truncating the largest eigenvectors improves contact prediction (Qin 2018).
validation_type: CONTACTS and generative capacity only. NO study validates the collective modes against functional or experimental coupling. This is the method's central weakness for an allostery claim.
kinase_evidence: Not applied to kinases in the eigenmode form. Closest kinase precedent is statistical-energy decomposition of a kinase Potts model: DFG-out propensity predicted and validated against structural propensities and binding affinities, with activation-loop/alphaC/HRD interactions identified as the dominant contributors (Haldane 2016; Haldane 2018), extended to a TYROSINE-KINASE-specific conformational-landscape analysis (Gizzio 2022; Gizzio 2024).
feasibility: Trivial and measured: eigh on the 5313x5313 (Lq) coupling matrix ran in 11.2 s at 0.75 GB peak on this machine. J tensor is 112 MB.
inputs: FULL J tensor (recoverable from the .plmc file). Gauge fixing to zero-sum/Ising gauge is mandatory first.
failure_modes: (i) The eigenspectrum of J is GAUGE-DEPENDENT - plmc's output gauge must be fixed explicitly or the modes are meaningless. (ii) lambda_J = 1.0 shrinks small couplings preferentially and therefore distorts exactly the low-eigenvalue tail that Cocco 2013 identifies as contact-like; regularisation strength is known to reshape Potts parameters (Haldane 2019). (iii) Eigendecomposing an already-fitted plmDCA J is a descriptive spectral analysis, not the reduced-rank inference that Cocco 2013 and Shimagaki 2019 actually performed - do not present it as a Hopfield-Potts fit. (iv) Shimagaki 2019 reports the collective patterns cluster sequences into functional SUBFAMILIES, so a 'collective mode' may be a clade label rather than allostery.
hostile_reviewer: 'Your collective modes are phylogeny' (Qin 2018; Shimagaki 2019); 'the spectrum is gauge- and regularisation-dependent'; 'no one has shown these modes are allosteric'. Report as descriptive decomposition with the clade-correlation of each top mode shown.
cost_benefit: Cheap and informative as a supplement; not load-bearing. Run it, label it descriptive, and do not build a central claim on it.

method: Subfamily-differential coupling (ErbB vs broader TK; specificity-determining positions)
verdict: SKIP as a computation; CITE in Discussion
improves_long_range: Plausibly, but the kinase evidence is for specificity rather than allostery per se: determinants of specificity in the kinome form sparse networks of NON-CONSERVED residues spanning distant regions, three experimentally validated (alphaC1, alphaC3, APE-7), implying inter-residue allostery in specificity and evolutionary decoupling of activity from specificity (Creixell 2015). Generic method with functional support: nested coevolution separates inter-clade from intra-clade coupling, improves contact prediction in shallow subsamples, and yields sectors that are more spatially compact and enriched for activity-disrupting mutations (Colavin 2022).
validation_type: MIXED. Creixell 2015 is experimental (three DoS validated in cells). Colavin 2022 is contacts plus enrichment for activity-disrupting mutations.
kinase_evidence: Strong but for a different question (Creixell 2015, human kinome; Gizzio 2022/2024, TK vs STK conformational landscape validated by 108 FEP simulations).
feasibility: Compute is cheap (one extra plmc refit) but the STATISTICS are the blocker. Four human ErbB paralogs; even a metazoa-wide ErbB alignment yields at most a few thousand sequences. Haldane 2019 shows contact and epistasis predictions degrade fastest as N falls and that overfitting is negligible only above a few thousand effective sequences, so an ErbB-only refit sits at or below the edge of defensibility.
inputs: Raw MSA with subfamily labels + new plmc refits (new J tensors) + depth-matched bootstrap subsamples of the parent alignment.
failure_modes: Differences between two separately regularised fits at different N_eff are dominated by sampling noise; phylogenetic stratification is confounded with subfamily by construction; requires depth-matched bootstrap controls that will likely consume the whole signal.
hostile_reviewer: 'Your ErbB-specific couplings are a small-sample artifact of a shallow sub-alignment' - and at ErbB depth this is probably correct.
cost_benefit: Negative at ErbB depth. A TK-vs-STK split would be better powered but is a different paper (and largely already done by Gizzio 2022/2024).

method: Restricted Boltzmann machines on MSAs (extended constitutive motifs)
improves_long_range: Not demonstrated for this question. RBM features are interpretable and map to tertiary contacts, extended secondary motifs, disordered regions, function/ligand specificity AND phylogenetic identity across 20 families (Tubiana 2019), but no benchmark shows RBMs beat DCA at recovering long-range functional coupling.
validation_type: Interpretability and generative design; no functional-coupling benchmark. Related model-comparison work ranks the pairwise Potts model ABOVE a VAE on generative capacity (McGee 2021), i.e. extra capacity is not automatically an improvement.
kinase_evidence: NONE retrieved. No published RBM analysis of a kinase family surfaced in these searches.
feasibility: Trainable on CPU at L=253, q=21, N=32,672 (input dimension 5313) but hyperparameter selection - hidden-unit count, sparsity regularisation, schedule - is the real cost and each PCD training run is hours without a GPU; multiple runs needed for stability. Flag as the only method here with a material compute burden.
failure_modes: No principled mapping from a hidden unit to a residue PAIR, so it cannot directly answer 'is pair i-j allosterically coupled'. Features explicitly mix phylogeny with function (Tubiana 2019). Stochastic training creates a reproducibility burden. No agreed significance null.
hostile_reviewer: 'What is the null, how many hidden units did you try, and how is a hidden unit an allosteric coupling?' All three are currently unanswerable.
cost_benefit: Negative. Highest cost, weakest evidence, no kinase precedent, and it expands reviewer attack surface without adding support.
